report_name: Exposed Credentials Give Attackers a Major Head Start, Report Finds

attack_patterns.name: Credentials from Password Stores
attack_patterns.description: Infostealer malware exfiltrates saved credentials from browsers, VPN clients, and other applications on infected user devices. According to the report, attackers then purchase these credentials and use them for initial access (T1078 - Valid Accounts) via public-facing applications (T1133 - External Remote Services) to deploy ransomware.

attack_patterns.name: Valid Accounts
attack_patterns.description: Attackers use credentials exposed by data breaches or infostealer malware to gain initial access to corporate networks.

attack_patterns.name: External Remote Services
attack_patterns.description: Attackers use compromised credentials to log into corporate networks via external remote services like VPN or RDP.

malware.name: RedLine
malware.description: A specific infostealer malware mentioned in the report that infects user devices to exfiltrate saved credentials, which are then sold on the dark web.

malware.name: Infostealer Malware
malware.description: A class of malware that exfiltrates saved credentials from browsers, VPN clients, and other applications on infected devices. These credentials are then sold in logs on the dark web, enabling attackers to gain initial access to corporate networks.

infrastructure.name: Infostealer Marketplaces
infrastructure.description: Dark web marketplaces where logs from infostealer malware, containing compromised credentials, are sold in bulk to other attackers.
